sources: ComputeRasterMinMax with approximate disabled reads all pixels for exact range and excludes nodata.
When approximate is allowed cached extrema or a subsample of blocks may be trusted.
ComputeRasterMinMaxLocation does not specify which location is returned when extrema occur in several locations.
Min/max location ignores nodata-matching or mask-band invalid pixels.
GetMinimum success flag indicates whether a returned value is a tight minimum.
GetMaximum success flag indicates whether a returned value is a tight maximum.
Approximate statistics may use overviews or a subset of image tiles.
Computed statistics are generally stored back on the raster band.
Dataset ClearStatistics can clear cached statistics before independent replay.
--min-max computes minimum and maximum; --stats uses all pixels while --approx-stats is separate.
-mm forces computation of actual min/max values for each band.
-approx_stats may use overviews or only a subset of tiles and is not precise terminal evidence.
Python ComputeRasterMinMax defaults approx_ok to false, meaning all pixels are read.
Python ComputeMinMaxLocation inherits unspecified selection among multiple equal extrema.
Pixel-info reports raw and unscaled values for queried pixels.
Pixel-info can explicitly select an overview; terminal replay must remain on native resolution.
Unscaled value equals scaled raw value times scale plus offset.
Many input types default to Float32 output during unscale, so terminal precision must be explicitly controlled.
GDAL masks use zero for invalid and normally 255 for valid pixels.
Mask flags distinguish all-valid, per-dataset, alpha and nodata-derived masks.
A corresponding .msk file is used as the mask band before generated nodata or alpha fallbacks.
DropCache forces subsequent block requests back through the underlying driver.
Rasterio read_masks uses GDAL polarity: nonzero usually 255 is valid and zero is invalid.
MaskedArray mask polarity is inverse: True means invalid.
Rasterio documents the identity between inverted masked-array mask and read_masks for a band.
Dataset mask precedence gives .msk, alpha or internal mask priority before nodata-derived fallbacks.
Low valid values can be rounded to a nodata sentinel in narrowed 8-bit data; value alone may be ambiguous.
block_shapes exposes native storage blocks and block_windows yields their windows.
Window reads consume entire underlying chunks intersecting the requested window.
block_windows yields block row/column index and the dataset window used for reading.
Bands need not share block structure, so identical block-shape assumptions must be tested.
subdivide creates non-overlapping subwindows covering a window, useful for independent chunk replay.
round_window_to_full_blocks expands a window to full intersecting storage blocks and is not terminal parcel membership.
Masked arrays combine data and a boolean mask; True entries are invalid and excluded by masked computations.
The inverse mask or compressed method can retrieve valid entries only.
masked_invalid masks NaN and infinite values.
argmin returns only the first occurrence when a minimum value occurs multiple times.
nonzero returns indices of all true/nonzero elements in row-major C-style order.
flatnonzero returns every nonzero index in the flattened input.
isinf identifies positive and negative infinity independently of NaN.
isfinite is true only for values that are neither infinity nor NaN.
NumPy follows IEEE 754 and NaN is distinct from positive or negative infinity.
ComputeRasterMinMaxLocation can return a warning when there are no valid values.
Exact ComputeRasterMinMax scans the complete band rather than sampled blocks.
GetStatistics may return pre-existing STATISTICS metadata rather than scanning if forced computation is not required.
The modern raster-info --stats mode is documented as using all pixels.
When a .msk sidecar exists Rasterio ignores nodata metadata values and bases masks on the sidecar.
Reading with masked=True returns a NumPy MaskedArray carrying invalid-pixel state.
GDAL-style 0/255 masks and NumPy boolean masks require explicit polarity normalization.
compressed returns a one-dimensional array, so coordinate provenance must be retained separately.
Masked-array slices can share mask views, so mutation-sensitive terminal logic should avoid altering source masks.
GDAL one-location API insufficient for ties
ComputeMinMaxLocation supplies one min and one max location and explicitly leaves multi-hit choice unspecified.
block_windows iteration is left-to-right and top-to-bottom, enabling a canonical replay order.
GetMaskBand always returns a mask band, including all-valid fallback when no invalidity source exists.
Pixel-info reports resolved column and line together with raw/unscaled value for independent extrema-coordinate spot checks.
